# 21. Meeting Notes — Presentation Requirements and Accessibility Tool Discussion (unverified transcript)

**Source:** auto-generated meeting summary, Sept 5 2026 23:13–23:21, two unnamed speakers ("Speaker 1–2"). **Not verified against a recording or by the team — treat as a rough transcript of a real conversation, not a settled decision.** Captured here because it sets concrete logistics for the pitch (time limit, running order) and adds two framing points not yet written down elsewhere: a hardware-analogy argument for "adaptive input," and an explicit correction against over-selling the AI angle.

---

## What was discussed

**Time limit and structure.** Speaker 2 confirmed the segment is a hard **15 minutes total — presentation, demo, and Q&A combined**. Proposed running order: (1) a quick live app demo first, (2) context — how the app was built and its current state, (3) the core problem it solves, plus stating the project is open source with no revenue model. This is a **demo-first** structure, the opposite of treating the demo as the closing proof.

**Existing tools work for one impairment at a time.** The plan is to first show that tools like TalkBack/Narrator or Voice Access work fine for someone with a single, clean impairment — particularly if they can still use a keyboard well or have reliable speech-to-text. Only after establishing that do they introduce the actual gap: **combinations** of impairments, where no existing tool's single assumed capability point matches the user. This is the same framing already locked in [01 — Problem](01-problem.md) §1.2 ("the long tail of ability combinations that fixed-point tools ignore," explicitly *not* "2+ diagnoses" as the framing) — this meeting is about how to *demonstrate* that point on stage (show a tool succeeding, then show it fail), not a change to the framing itself.

**Hardware analogy for "adaptive input."** Speaker 2 introduced a concrete pitch device: adaptive input by routing control through whatever body part a person can actually use already exists — as **hardware**. Examples given: a **foot-controlled trackball** for someone without hand use, and a **tongue-controlled mouse** ("tongue mouse") for paralyzed users. The argument is: this project does the same adaptive-body-part idea **in software, on a commodity phone/laptop**, with no dedicated device to buy or fit. This is a new, specific comparison — not previously written down — but it's consistent with, and strengthens, the existing hardware-cost argument in [14 — Market Research](14-market-research.md) (dedicated AAC/access hardware like Tobii Dynavox or the Xbox Adaptive Controller costing thousands of dollars; see also [tech/research/01 — Input Methods](../tech/research/01-input-methods.md) on the Xbox Adaptive Controller as fusion precedent). **Caveat:** the specific product names ("foot trackball," "tongue mouse") are as spoken in the meeting and have not been independently verified/cited here — treat as a pitch talking point, not a sourced claim, until someone checks the actual product names and specs.

**Correction: this is not primarily an AI product.** Speaker 2 flagged and pushed back on a misconception — that this is "an AI-based accessibility tool." It isn't: the core is **adaptive input** (the capability profile driving which input surface renders), and AI/agent features are deliberately narrow, not the headline. This restates, for the pitch specifically, the same decision already made and documented in [17 — Meeting Notes: Tree Simplification](17-meeting-notes-tree-simplification.md) ("decided not to make this unnecessarily AI-powered or agentic") — worth repeating here because it's easy for a demo audience to *assume* "adaptive + agent" means "AI-first" unless the pitch says otherwise out loud.

**UI accessibility.** The app's own UI should be built accessibly — accessibility-tooling-compatible — and input modes should only be shown/offered in the screen regions calibration found accessible to that user. This matches a decision already implemented in [code/app](../../code/app/README.md) ("output goes where input cannot" — the output strip is placed in the least-reachable region) — this meeting extends the same logic to input-mode visibility generally, not just the output strip. No doc currently states this as a general UI rule; flagged below as a gap.

## Tasks (unassigned to real names — speaker numbers only)

1. **Design the UI to be accessible** — primarily accessibility-feature-compatible, input modes shown only in accessible screen areas. *Partially done*: [code/app](../../code/app/README.md) already places the output strip by reachability; the general "only show input modes where they're operable" rule is new and not yet written into [03 — Input & Calibration](03-input-calibration.md) or the app code.
2. **Finalize the input layer and mapping** so the system is controlled directly from a phone. *Largely done* — see [code/app/README.md](../../code/app/README.md): calibration, the 3×4 task/method matrix, and touch+voice fusion are built. What remains unbuilt (and out of scope for this event per [05 — Locked Scope](05-scope.md)) is anything downstream of the phone — an agent, a browser tree, a real target app.
3. **Demo existing tools (TalkBack/Narrator, Voice Access) live or via clip** to show single-impairment success before showing the combination-impairment gap. Reflected in [presentation/notes/demo-clips.md](../../presentation/notes/demo-clips.md) (clips 1–2), now noted there as demoable live instead of only pre-recorded.
4. **State the open-source / no-revenue-model positioning** in the pitch. Already the subject of [14 — Market Research](14-market-research.md) §5/§6/§10; now also pulled earlier into the pitch's context section, not just the close.
5. **Prepare the presentation** — demo, context, problem, within the 15-minute limit including Q&A. Reflected in the restructured [presentation/notes/outline.md](../../presentation/notes/outline.md).

## How this connects to the rest of the docs

None of this changes locked scope in [05 — Scope](05-scope.md): the hardware analogy (foot trackball, tongue mouse) is a **pitch comparison**, not a request to build foot- or tongue-based input — the event build stays touch/voice/vision on a phone, per existing scope. The "not an AI product" correction is not new policy either — it's [17](17-meeting-notes-tree-simplification.md)'s decision restated for a stage-audience context where it needs to be said explicitly rather than left implicit.

The one genuinely new, not-yet-elsewhere-documented item is the **general "only show input modes in accessible screen regions" UI rule** (item 1 above) — this is narrower than what's built (which only applies reachability logic to the output strip) and broader than a pitch talking point. Recommend folding it into [03 — Input & Calibration](03-input-calibration.md) or [code/app/README.md](../../code/app/README.md)'s "deliberate design decisions" list if the team wants to commit to it as a real UI rule, rather than leaving it stated only here.
